hypothesis: The implementation of containsAny likely iterates over the string using char-based indexing (e.g., charAt) rather than code-point-based indexing. Since supplementary characters are represented as surrogate pairs (two chars), the algorithm incorrectly matches individual surrogate components instead of the full character.

experiment_rationale: The failure occurs specifically with supplementary characters (surrogate pairs). reasoning_summary: The defect is in the procedural logic of the containsAny method. It fails to correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters because it likely treats them as individual 16-bit chars rather than single code points. This is a classic algorithmic error in string processing where the iteration strategy is insufficient for the data type (Unicode supplementary characters).

The bug report notes that standard JRE methods handle these characters correctly, implying the custom implementation in StringUtils is the source of the error.
